title: PoMtVRS: Preference-Optimized Multi-Task Vehicle Routing Solver with Preference Gating
claim: A plug-and-play gated decoder block plus pairwise preference optimization turns a multi-task solver into a stable, unified training pipeline.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, with nested modules and colored routing arrows
description: A wide, rounded blue-bordered diagram that reads left to right. On the left, a VRP instance panel shows a stacked label column (C, O, B, L, TW) plus a scatter of nodes with a red depot. Below it are task-type checkboxes (CVRP, VRPB, VRPLTW, VRPBTW). They feed an embedding stack, then an H_c box that splits into h_a, h_b and h_c. In the center, pastel-colored Encoder/Decoder pairs A, B and C sit inside a gray 'Backbone Models' box. Above them, a purple Preference-Gated Block runs Gated Attention, then State Mapping, then FFN & Norm, with colored lines feeding each decoder. On the right, a 'Preference Optimization' panel shows solution pairs with a preference sign, a BT Model cylinder and a PO Loss funnel, with an arrow labelled Action Probabilities. Far right, four colored tiles show routing outputs for CVRP, VRPB, VRPBTW and VRPLTW.
caption: An overview of the proposed PoMtVRS. It integrates seamlessly into typical encoder-decoder frameworks: Under the unified VRP environment, PoMtVRS augments standard neural solvers by inserting a Preference-Gated Block (PGB) into the decoder, which enhances decoder representation and adaptively refines attention context. Training adopts preference optimization (PO), which replaces scalarized rewards by transforming intra-instance pairwise preferences into a Bradley-Terry (BT) likelihood and PO loss, yielding a stable reward signal to optimize the PL policy.
abstract: Multi-task vehicle routing solvers via deep reinforcement learning have attracted broad attention and achieved significant progress in handling multiple constraints. However, existing neural solvers still face critical challenges, including insufficient representation, unstable training, and inefficient exploration in large combinatorial action spaces, which often prevents performance from meeting its full potential. To address these issues, we propose PoMtVRS (Preference-Optimized Multi-Task Vehicle Routing Solver with Preference Gating), a plug-and-play framework that jointly improves decoder representations and exploration efficiency through a synergistic combination of decoder-side augmentation and preference-driven optimization. Specifically, we introduce the preference optimization objective to learn relative comparisons among candidate solutions for different routing tasks, encouraging a higher generation probability of better solutions. Meanwhile, we design a preference-gated block that adaptively modulates decoder representations via sparse gated attention and nonlinear residual refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PoMtVRS elevates state-of-the-art unified neural VRP backbones, achieving leading performance in multi-task benchmarks and stronger generalization.
